decisions.summary: _unkinked: a returning leg under 40 ft (HAIRPIN_LEG_FT) is cut, keeping the longer arm
decisions.why: 0081 drawing page verbatim: 'where a lane turns back on itself, a returning leg under 40 ft is cut'; the implementation moves to the research (FR-004).

decisions.summary: _unkinked: a hairpin whose returning leg is 40 ft or more 'now stands' (returns [p] unchanged); the test pins _unkinked(long_back) == [long_back]
decisions.why: 0081's own rule opens 'A lane never doubles back in a hairpin. A turn of more than 140 degrees is a hairpin'; the page never says a longer returning leg stands - that is the plan completing the page's thought from 'under 40 ft is cut'. It also does not do what the plan says: measured 2026-10-08 by a scratch probe through make test-file (lane [(0,50),(200,50),(150,55)], 50 ft returning leg), settle_shapes returns 1 change every round with the lane unchanged (so the settle never settles and burns all SETTLE_ROUNDS), law.lanes_that_kink still names it, and last_resort.lane_violators names it, so the last resort drops the WHOLE lane (or refuse_unreached refuses the map). The page's 40 ft rule is honored only by cutting more than the page cuts. The case the page does not settle - what a 140-degree turn with a returning leg of 40 ft or more becomes - must be settled by the feature's own route (FR-003 E4 research first, or the FR-004 exception path recorded on 0081), never by leaving a hairpin the page forbids or by a silent whole-lane drop.

decisions.summary: _unkinked: a zigzag is pulled straight - vertices ka..kb dropped, one lane from the vertex before the first turn to the vertex after the second
decisions.why: 0081 verbatim: 'Two turns of more than 50 degrees within 40 ft of path, about a dozen paces, are pulled straight'; the old cut left two lanes.

decisions.summary: settle_shapes (row 490) closes by calling the fixed _unkinked
decisions.why: Its finding is the same two 0081 sentences; it inherits W45-2's defect for the 40 ft-plus hairpin and is fixed with it.

decisions.summary: The behind-the-back-wall rule removed whole: law.ends_behind (and its LAW entry), the keeper's, tree end_faults', last resort's and Lawful's reads of it, settle_ends' carry round the gable and off_the_back, corridors.round_the_gable - including units impl-drift had ruled IN-STEP
decisions.why: 0246 drawing page: 'A lane end counts as reaching a farmhouse when it comes within 60 ft of the house, or within 12 ft of the steading's built ground'; no side is excluded and impl-drift's notes on rows 488-489 say the behind-the-house rule is not on 0246. ends_behind only ever flagged ends within WAY_END_REACH_FT of a house, so every end it flagged is one 0246 counts as reaching. Removing the law check with its repairs is the fix itself, not extra scope: leaving the check with no repair would send those lanes to the last resort.

decisions.summary: The settlement-side form (water_ways/lanes.py behind_house, reaches_dooryard, trim_lane_stubs) left for its own ranked rows
decisions.why: FR-006: a wave is a contiguous run of the ranking; those rows are ranked, in scope ('kept') and taken in their turn, not deferred or excepted.

decisions.summary: Occasions: none - the five hamlets regenerated 2026-10-08 with byte-identical manifests
decisions.why: A dated one-shot measurement deciding the occasion per feature 294; asserts nothing the request or spec does not ask.

decisions.summary: Tests restated: behind-the-house tests replaced by 'an end behind a house reaches it and is left'; the tree's third-end case rebuilt nearer house A
decisions.why: Tests that enforce the fixed behavior serve the request; the rebuilt tree case keeps the third-end rule tested without the removed rule.
